title: Choose a launch strategy
question: For the next release, should we run an invite-only pilot, a public beta, or a staged regional rollout?

criteria.label: Learning value
criteria.description: Higher scores mean more actionable feedback from the intended audience.

criteria.label: Operational readiness
criteria.description: Higher scores mean a more manageable support and reliability burden.

criteria.label: Audience reach
criteria.description: Higher scores mean broader access for potential users in this launch window.

learning.note: Illustrative estimate: interviews with a small cohort may generate detailed feedback.

readiness.note: Assumes the team can personally support a capped cohort.

reach.note: Illustrative low reach score for an invitation-only release.

learning.note: Illustrative estimate: more diverse users, but feedback quality could vary.

readiness.note: Assumes open enrollment creates substantial support and incident risk.

reach.note: Illustrative high reach score; not a forecast of acquisition or conversion.

learning.note: Illustrative estimate: regional feedback may be useful but less representative.

readiness.note: Assumes feature gates and rollback procedures are ready before launch.

reach.note: Illustrative middle reach score for limited geographic availability.

assumptions: This is a fictional, illustrative example. No scores or ranges are factual measurements.
All criteria are oriented so higher is better and use a shared 0–10 preference scale.
Options are assessed for the same release window, staffing level, and budget.
Criterion contributions are additive; interactions and changing scores are not modeled.
